pr_body:
This removes SQL's use of `org.elasticsearch.Version` class and usages replaced by `SqlVersion`.

All the currently considered released versions (`7.0.0` to `8.16.0`) have been declared as `SqlVersion` instances. These are still tested against.

The last "known release" (`8.16.0`) is considered the "server compatibility version" and all clients at or past this release are compatible with the server; notably, they can be also on a newer version than server's. 
Clients released before this "server compatibility version" respect existing compatibility requirements (must/can be older up to one major lower, but past `7.7.0`).
The "server compatibility version" will not be updated with newer stack releases (at least not until #112745 is addressed).

Fixes #102689
pr_comment:
Thanks for checking the draft, @rjernst.

> There can't be any concept of semantic versioning anymore

That's clear.
But just to add a clarification of the intent: the clients that the change is meant for are (still) released part of the stack only. They've been using the SemVer version and will continue to do so. No updates to them are intended besides fixes; i.e. no new features, that require a new version-dependent serialisation / answer format.
If this status will ever be updated, we'll need to evolve the versioning mechanism (in SQL); but right now, a simple translation should do. 
But your point about only using a weakly monotonically increasing ID is clear and I'll update the PR.
This still parses `Build.current().version()`. Why can't the latest version simply be the highest id in `SqlVersions`?

> This still parses Build.current().version(). Why can't the latest version simply be the highest id in SqlVersions?

This is mostly used for error reporting on non-SL (and JDBC tests). Those stack release releases could just use the highest ID in SqlVersions, but it could be confusing for non-SL users.

In that case, you need to use a mechanism similar to `TransportVersion.toReleaseVersion` (using the `ReleaseVersions` class) - have a csv or other map mechanism to go from SqlVersion to release version

@thecoop 

> In that case, you need to use a mechanism similar to TransportVersion.toReleaseVersion (using the ReleaseVersions class) - have a csv or other map mechanism to go from SqlVersion to release version

That would map the same "final" 8.16.0 "SQL server compatibility version" to an ever increasing stack release version since, unlike the IndexVersion and TransportVersion, SqlVersion won't be updated anymore (again, at least not until #112745 is addressed).

I've removed the dependency on `Build.current()` further by adjusting the error message. There still are uses of it, but _only_ in tests. 

However, is also `Build` supposed to be removed at some point, besides `Version`? Is this the reason you're advising the above? If that's the case, I could introduce a mapping, or even just a text file to contain the latest release version (since no SqlVersion mapping is needed). But then the requirements should also be updated.
`Build` is not going away, it provides information on the current running build which is needed for diagnostics and info.

> That would map the same "final" 8.16.0 "SQL server compatibility version" to an ever increasing stack release version since, unlike the IndexVersion and TransportVersion, SqlVersion won't be updated anymore (again, at least not until https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112745 is addressed).

Pinning to the next version id shouldn't require SqlVersion be updated at all. That's the whole point of the new versioning model, it is decoupled from release versions (or places like serverless that have no release version).

If we pin at 8_16_00_00, then the clients can be updated (in the same release) to send that id from now on. And they will send that id forever (assuming, as you say, that no future sql changes will be made). But by pinning, _if_ a change is needed, it will be decoupled from release versions.

> I've removed the dependency on Build.current() further by adjusting the error message. There still are uses of it, but only in tests.

Thanks! That is a big improvement here. However, parsing the version in tests still doesn't work, it means we still can't run any of these tests in serverless.

> If we pin at 8_16_00_00, then the clients can be updated (in the same release) to send that id from now on.

The clients [still use the stack version](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/112094#issuecomment-2312397684), they're only released part of it and will use its ever increasing SemVer version. 

OTOH, the server is only aware of versions up to `8.16.0` and none further (i.e. with this change proposal), we won't update it unless we'll ever consider implementing #112745. So we'd no longer need a mapping (which would be a never updated `8_16_00_00` to `8.16.0` mapping). 

> parsing the version in tests still doesn't work, it means we still can't run any of these tests in serverless.

No server code uses `Build.current()` and no tests for it either. The tests that use `Build.current()` are client-side tests, i.e. JDBC and CLI. JDBC _API_ expects a major and minor release of the server-side code, which we test with a SemVer version (see [getDatabaseMajorVersion](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/sql/DatabaseMetaData.html#getDatabaseMajorVersion--)); and we do something similar for the CLI.

We're not running the client tests in serverless. In serverless we're only running integration server tests. 
Also, the serverless test for this PR [passed](https://buildkite.com/elastic/elasticsearch-serverless-es-pr-check/builds/123#01922ffa-6593-4868-9ef1-8aef0253056a).

@ryan, if you still think we should introduce this `8_16_00_00` to `8.16.0` mapping, I can do it, but it'd bring nothing we can't do without it, at least not without having the clients support a different versioning mechanism, which is deferred to #112745.

> The clients https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/112094#issuecomment-2312397684, they're only released part of it and will use its ever increasing SemVer version.

But do they _need_ to send the stack version starting in 8.16? My concern is that if, for whatever reason, we ever _do_ need to make a change to sql, we will still be stuck on "semver", and in fact, there will be tons of semver versions for which we have to then account for.

I don't feel that strongly, though. If @thecoop is good with the PR as-is, then I'm ok with moving forward.
This is basically there - just a few minor tweaks, and confirming the future removal of `SearchRequest(minCompatibleShardNode)`, then it'll be good.

> But do they need to send the stack version starting in 8.16? 

This would allow a 8.16+ client connecting to an old(er) server to receive from the server the proper error message.

> My concern is that if, for whatever reason, we ever do need to make a change to sql, we will still be stuck on "semver", and in fact, there will be tons of semver versions for which we have to then account for.

If we'll need to evolve SQL beyond minimal fixes, we'd need to make it serverless-compatible, so we'll be forced to change the existing "semver" compatibility mechanism.
Thank you @thecoop and @ryan for the patience and reviews and @luigidellaquila for the review!

review_comment: Ah, `SqlVersion` doesn't implement `VersionId`. If it implements `VersionId<T>` then this method will come for free
Right, there's no `.before()` method and `SqlVersion` can't implement `VersionId<T>`, since it's in a package very light in dependencies.

No further versions will be added.
Any clients on a version at or newer than this will be considered compatible with the server -- checked in `VersionCompatibility#hasVersioningIndependentFeatures`.
This change was unintended (an editor unintended action) and will be reverted, along with all similar others.
Does this still need to be reverted?
How will this be updated for further 8.15 patch releases?
It wouldn't be updated anymore. All 8.15.x release will behave as current 8.15.1.
Does it mean that if we have to patch 8.15 (pretty unlikely), we won't need a new version here?

main is now v9, which can only talk to 8.17 nodes (when released). Does this mean we can remove all these versions, or are these actually _client_ versions which still need to be compatible? Is this documented somewhere?

> Is this documented somewhere?

The  the current version compatibility policy has been documented [here](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/sql-jdbc.html#jdbc-compatibility). This has been applying to the 7.x and 8.x.

Given the SQL maintenance status, this PR proposes updating this policy by allowing unrestricted connectivity between clients and servers past 8.16 (comment [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/112094/files#diff-35b51352875c23b3a8029fab7ad54b93bb9363c8d5a14bfd61992a534a3e86edR28-R32)). Any pre-8.16 releases (including all 8.15 releases to follow) will have to comply with the exiting policy (linked above).
The SL releases will be considered at version 8.16 (the "server compatibility version").

> Does this mean we can remove all these versions.

The versions should remain in the 8.x branch, but those 7.x not referenced explicitly in `VersionCompatibility` class (I think it's just `SqlVersions.V_7_12_0`) could be removed on 9.x. I think this would be done after back porting to 8.x though.

> are these actually client versions which still need to be compatible?

Yes, the post 7.7.0 client releases would need to stay compatible with 8.x servers.

> those 7.x not referenced explicitly in VersionCompatibility class (I think it's just SqlVersions.V_7_12_0) could be removed on 9.x

This could be an `@UpdateForV9` tag on the 7.0.0 version/SqlVersion class.

I think it's worth a descriptive comment at this point, that no further versions should be added in the normal course of things.

This is the `minCompatibleShardNode` - which is still a `Version`. If the version is locked at 8.16, this means this parameter can be completely removed on v9 and replaced with another mechanism if/when SQL needs to be updated?

> this means this parameter can be completely removed on v9

I would think so, assuming that we have an upgrade procedure to 9.x similar to [the existing 7.x to 8.x one](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elastic-stack/current/upgrading-elastic-stack.html#prepare-to-upgrade): upgrade to the latest 8.x one and then the target 9.x. This would mean that the SearchRequest wouldn't need to be given a min (shard) version, since all the nodes in the cluster would respect that condition already.

> and replaced with another mechanism if/when SQL needs to be updated?

I think the above would stand independent on SQL being updated or not.
OK - After this is merged, I'll look at removing that then
